name: yara_scan
description: Sweep a file or directory with a YARA rule file the caller names, and report where each rule matched: rule, file, and per string match the identifier, offset and length. A rule match says the rule's condition held, not that the file is malicious. SENSITIVE: yara -s prints the bytes a string matched, so a rule that finds a password or a key puts it in the output; the answer carries no matched bytes at all, and yara's text is read as a stream and dropped. write_matches: true writes them (as yara prints them) to $OUT/yara-matched-strings.jsonl, mode 0600, one row per string match with the answer's finding_id, only when this runs as a job (run it with secret_output: true) and refused anywhere else. Warnings and errors are kept whole in a stderr file; a run stopped by its time limit says complete: false and keeps what was read; status is complete, partial or failed with yara's exit status. It records the rules file's sha256 and yara's version; links inside a scanned directory are not followed where yara has -N. No rules ship with it.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to let yara run (default 60, at most 110); a run that is stopped keeps what it printed

limit.description: Rule matches and string matches shown inline, each (default 200, an inline page size); every one is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in the page's all_results

write_matches.description: Write the matched bytes to $OUT/yara-matched-strings.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a value
